topic.subject: social
topic.title: Rural and urban livelihoods
topic.scope: farm and non-farm work, landless labourers, street vendors, permanent and casual work

misconceptions.statement: All farmers in India own the land they cultivate.
misconceptions.why: Students often generalize from stories of wealthy landowners in media.
misconceptions.fix: Many rural workers are landless labourers who work on others' fields for daily wages.

probe.question: Who does a landless labourer work for?
probe.wrong_answer: They work on their own small plot of land.

misconceptions.statement: Farmers have work throughout the entire year.
misconceptions.why: Students assume work is a continuous process like school or office jobs.
misconceptions.fix: Farming is seasonal; labourers often face unemployment during the months between sowing and harvesting.

probe.question: What do farm labourers do during the off-season?
probe.wrong_answer: They continue working on the same farm every day.

misconceptions.root_belief: work is always a continuous activity
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver children's ideas in social science

misconceptions.statement: Street vendors are always poor because they are lazy.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse economic status with personal character traits.
misconceptions.fix: Street vendors work very hard but lack permanent shops and face daily uncertainty.

probe.question: Why do street vendors work on the sidewalk?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they do not want to work hard in a shop.

misconceptions.root_belief: poverty is a result of personal failure

misconceptions.statement: All city jobs provide medical leave and pensions.
misconceptions.why: Students project the benefits of their parents' or teachers' jobs onto all urban work.
misconceptions.fix: Only permanent, formal jobs offer benefits; casual workers have no such security.

probe.question: Does a daily wage worker get paid sick leave?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all city workers get paid leave.

misconceptions.root_belief: my experience is the universal experience

misconceptions.statement: Farm work is only done by men.
misconceptions.why: Students see men ploughing and selling in images and stories, and overlook women's daily field labour.
misconceptions.fix: Women and men both do farm work: sowing, transplanting, weeding and harvesting. Women do a large share of it, often without recognition or equal pay.

probe.question: Who does the work of transplanting paddy and harvesting in a village?
probe.wrong_answer: Only men do it; women stay at home.

misconceptions.root_belief: Gender roles strictly divide who does productive work

misconceptions.statement: Everyone in a village works in farming.
misconceptions.why: Villages are strongly linked with fields and crops, so students assume no other work exists there.
misconceptions.fix: Villages also have non-farm work such as weaving, pottery, shopkeeping, teaching, carpentry, tailoring and running small shops.

probe.question: Name a person in a village who does not work on a farm. What do they do?
probe.wrong_answer: There is no such person; everyone in a village is a farmer.

misconceptions.source_hint: research on children's conceptions of rural life

misconceptions.statement: Street vendors do not need to work hard or buy anything because they sell for free on the road.
misconceptions.why: Students see vendors on open pavements with no shop, so they think there is no cost or effort.
misconceptions.fix: Street vendors buy goods from wholesale markets, carry or arrange them, stand for long hours and sell in all weather. They may also pay fees or face being moved away.

probe.question: Where does a fruit seller on the street get the fruit he sells?
probe.wrong_answer: He gets it free from nowhere, so he has no cost.

misconceptions.root_belief: No shop means no investment or effort

misconceptions.statement: Formal jobs mean only government jobs.
misconceptions.why: Students link permanent salaried work only with government offices, police and schools.
misconceptions.fix: Formal jobs have fixed pay, fixed hours and written terms. They exist in government offices and also in many private companies and factories.

probe.question: Does a worker in a big private company with a fixed salary and contract have a formal job?
probe.wrong_answer: No, only government workers have formal jobs.

misconceptions.statement: Landless labourers are people who do not work.
misconceptions.why: The word 'landless' is read as having nothing to do, since they have no farm of their own.
misconceptions.fix: Landless labourers work on other people's fields for daily or seasonal wages. They do the hard farm work but do not own the land.

probe.question: What do landless labourers do for a living?
probe.wrong_answer: Nothing, because they have no land to farm.

misconceptions.statement: Farming work is the same amount in every month, so farmers earn the same all year.
misconceptions.why: Students do not link crop cycles like sowing and harvesting to periods of heavy and light work.
misconceptions.fix: Farm work is heavy during sowing and harvest and light in between. Many farm families earn mainly after harvest and look for other work in the slack months.

probe.question: Why do many farm families look for other work or migrate in some months?
probe.wrong_answer: Farming gives the same work every month, so they leave only for fun.

misconceptions.root_belief: Work and income are constant across seasons

misconceptions.statement: Self-employed people in villages always have an employer who pays them a salary.
misconceptions.why: Students think everyone who works is paid a monthly wage by some boss.
misconceptions.fix: Self-employed people such as potters, tailors and shopkeepers run their own work. They buy materials, sell goods or services, and their earnings depend on customers.

probe.question: Who pays a village potter for the pots he makes and sells?
probe.wrong_answer: His employer pays him a fixed monthly salary.

misconceptions.root_belief: All workers are paid salaries by employers

misconceptions.statement: Casual labourers in cities have a regular job with a fixed monthly salary.
misconceptions.why: Students think anyone doing city work, like construction, has the same steady pay as an office worker.
misconceptions.fix: Casual labourers, such as construction workers, are hired for a day or a short job and paid daily wages. They have no fixed pay, no long-term contract and may wait at labour chowks for work.

probe.question: How is a construction worker who stands at a labour chowk paid?
probe.wrong_answer: He gets a fixed monthly salary and is sure of work every day.

misconceptions.root_belief: All city work is steady salaried work
